I added `withoutHost` as a stub at the end of `src/utils.ts`. Its body only throws "not implemented", and its doc comment and `@example` follow the style of `withoutFragment` next to it. Every existing export is unchanged. The spec says no new types or constants are exported, so none were added. `src/index.ts` already picks the function up through its `export * from "./utils"`. `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports no errors, and `npx vitest run` passes as before (13 files, 424 tests).

**Decision for you:** I wrote the signature as `withoutHost(input: string): string`, with an explicit return type. The ticket's line, `export function withoutHost(input: string);`, can't be the stub as written: with no body it is an incomplete declaration and won't compile. And if I gave it the throwing body without a return type, TypeScript would infer `void`, so any type-level test expecting `string` would fail. The spec's decision list rejects adding the `: string` annotation, but callers see the same `string` type either way. The implementer can drop the annotation once the real body is in, and the type will still come out as `string`.

Exported names added: `withoutHost`

I wrote the suite in `test/ufo-without-host.test.ts`. It covers all 15 scenarios in the spec, with flat `test` calls from `vitest` and `expect(...).toBe(...)` as in `test/punycode.test.ts`.

**Checks:**
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports no errors. However, `tsconfig.json` only includes `src`, so this command doesn't type-check the test file.
- `npx vitest run test/ufo-without-host.` runs 33 tests and all 33 fail. That's expected, because `withoutHost` still throws `not implemented`.
- Before writing the tests, I ran every spec example that wasn't simple through the formula the spec gives, `(parseURL(input).pathname || "/") + search + hash`. Each one gave the output the spec states, so the expected values should be right.

**What's covered:**
- Each scenario has a happy-path test and a boundary test, keyed by its kind and position: happy-1 to happy-3, boundary-1 to boundary-10, unhappy-1 and unhappy-2. Every example row in the spec's tables is asserted.
- Inputs are written as JavaScript strings, so the spec's literal backslashes are doubled: `https:\\example.com\foo\bar` becomes `"https:\\\\example.com\\foo\\bar"`.
- The `[happy-2]` tests import from `../src` as well as `../src/utils`, because that scenario is about the package entry point. One of them checks that the entry point exports the very same function.
- `[happy-1]` also checks that calling the function twice gives the same result and leaves the input unchanged. `[boundary-8]` checks that the empty string doesn't throw.

Only the test file was added; nothing else in the repository changed.

33 tests, in 1 file.

I wrote the hidden suite in `test/hidden-ufo-without-host/without-host.test.ts`. All 34 tests fail against the current stub, which throws `not implemented`. To check the expected values, I ran a copy of the file against a reference implementation built from the spec's definition, `(parsed.pathname || "/") + parsed.search + parsed.hash`. All 34 passed. That copy lives in `$TMPDIR` and no file outside the test folder changed. `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports no errors.

Every public test has at least one hidden test extending it, named in a comment above the test. The suite covers all 15 scenario keys (`happy-1..3`, `boundary-1..10`, `unhappy-1..2`). It targets these shortcuts:

- **Hard-coding or a simple regex strip:** other schemes (`ftp:`, `git+ssh:`), IPv6 hosts with credentials, and an `@` inside the path.
- **Searching for the first `/` after the host:** `https://example.com?q=1/x` → `/?q=1/x` and `https://example.com#a/b` → `/#a/b`.
- **Using `URL` or normalising:** malformed escapes such as `%E0%A4%A` and `e%zz` must come back unchanged, as must `///`, `/foo/?` and `/foo#`. Case and encoding must not change.
- **Converting backslashes only in the path:** backslashes in the query and hash of a URL with a host also become `/`. Mixed `:/\` forms are covered too.
- **Ignoring only spaces at the start:** tabs, newlines, several NULs, and NULs mixed with spaces before the protocol.
- **Calling `trim()` or adding a leading slash:** `"  /x"` stays `"  /x"`, and `foo.com/bar`, `example.com`, `./a`, `../x` and `a\b\c` come back unchanged.
- **Handling only the visible special protocols:** `vbscript:` and uppercase `DATA:`, `?` and `#` inside `javascript:`/`data:`/`blob:` input kept as part of the result, and leading whitespace or NUL before a script protocol.
- **Handling only `mailto:` and `tel:`:** `urn:`, `sms:` with a query, `news:`, and `CUSTOM:/…?x#y` all give `/`.
- **Special-casing only lowercase `file:///C:`:** `FILE:///`, `d:`, `file://localhost/...`, `file:///`, and a second drive letter whose slash must be kept.
- **Unwanted idempotency:** calling the function on its own result repeatedly (`//foo//bar//baz` → `//bar//baz` → `//baz` → `/`).

34 tests, in 1 file.

Open in the spec: none
